# Purpose

This document carries out the design-based analysis of the realised stratified sample from Section C. It estimates the mean monthly number of pages printed or photocopied per student, its variance, standard error, 95% confidence interval, coefficient of variation and design effect. It also compares the design-based results with a naive analysis that ignores the sampling design and with an approximately equal-sized SRSWOR sample.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE)
```


```{r load-data}
population <- read.csv(
  "wits_printing_population_with_auxiliary.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

sample_data <- read.csv(
  "wits_printing_sample.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cat("Population size:", nrow(population), "\n")
cat("Stratified sample size:", nrow(sample_data), "\n")

stopifnot(nrow(population) == 10000)
stopifnot(nrow(sample_data) == 414)
```

# 2. Verify required variables

```{r verify-variables}
required_sample_vars <- c(
  "student_id",
  "faculty",
  "pages_month",
  "N_h",
  "n_h",
  "inclusion_probability",
  "sampling_weight"
)

if (!all(required_sample_vars %in% names(sample_data))) {
  stop("The realised sample is missing one or more required variables.")
}

required_population_vars <- c(
  "student_id",
  "faculty",
  "pages_month"
)

if (!all(required_population_vars %in% names(population))) {
  stop("The population file is missing one or more required variables.")
}

cat("Required variables successfully verified.\n")
```

# 3. Known true finite-population quantities

Because this is a simulation study, the true finite-population mean can be calculated directly from all 10,000 population units.

```{r true-values}
true_mean <- mean(population$pages_month)
true_variance <- var(population$pages_month)
true_sd <- sd(population$pages_month)

cat("True finite-population mean:",
    round(true_mean, 2), "pages per month\n")
cat("True finite-population SD:",
    round(true_sd, 2), "pages\n")
cat("True finite-population variance:",
    round(true_variance, 2), "\n")
```

# 4. Design-based stratified estimate

For stratified random sampling, the estimator of the population mean is

```{r stratified-estimate}
N <- nrow(population)

faculty_stats <- aggregate(
  pages_month ~ faculty,
  data = sample_data,
  FUN = function(x) c(
    n = length(x),
    mean = mean(x),
    variance = var(x),
    sd = sd(x)
  )
)

faculty_stats
```

Create a clean stratum summary.

```{r clean-stratum-summary}
faculty_names <- unique(sample_data$faculty)

stratum_summary <- data.frame(
  faculty = faculty_names,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

stratum_summary$N_h <- sapply(
  stratum_summary$faculty,
  function(f) unique(sample_data$N_h[sample_data$faculty == f])
)

stratum_summary$n_h <- sapply(
  stratum_summary$faculty,
  function(f) unique(sample_data$n_h[sample_data$faculty == f])
)

stratum_summary$sample_mean <- sapply(
  stratum_summary$faculty,
  function(f) mean(sample_data$pages_month[sample_data$faculty == f])
)

stratum_summary$sample_variance <- sapply(
  stratum_summary$faculty,
  function(f) var(sample_data$pages_month[sample_data$faculty == f])
)

stratum_summary$sample_sd <- sqrt(stratum_summary$sample_variance)
stratum_summary$W_h <- stratum_summary$N_h / N
stratum_summary$f_h <- stratum_summary$n_h / stratum_summary$N_h

stratum_summary$sample_mean <- round(stratum_summary$sample_mean, 4)
stratum_summary$sample_variance <- round(stratum_summary$sample_variance, 4)
stratum_summary$sample_sd <- round(stratum_summary$sample_sd, 4)

stratum_summary
```

Calculate the weighted stratified mean.

```{r weighted-mean}
weighted_mean <- sum(
  stratum_summary$W_h *
    stratum_summary$sample_mean
)

cat("Design-based weighted mean:",
    round(weighted_mean, 4),
    "pages per month\n")
```

# 5. Estimated variance and standard error

For stratified random sampling without replacement,

```{r variance-se}
var_strat <- sum(
  stratum_summary$W_h^2 *
    (1 - stratum_summary$f_h) *
    (stratum_summary$sample_variance /
       stratum_summary$n_h)
)

se_strat <- sqrt(var_strat)

cat("Estimated variance:",
    round(var_strat, 6), "\n")
cat("Estimated standard error:",
    round(se_strat, 4),
    "pages\n")
```

# 6. 95% confidence interval

```{r confidence-interval}
z <- qnorm(0.975)

ci_lower <- weighted_mean - z * se_strat
ci_upper <- weighted_mean + z * se_strat
half_width <- z * se_strat

cat("95% CI: [",
    round(ci_lower, 3), ",",
    round(ci_upper, 3), "]\n")

cat("Confidence-interval half-width:",
    round(half_width, 3),
    "pages\n")

cat("Section B target half-width:",
    round(0.05 * true_mean, 3),
    "pages\n")
```

# 7. Coefficient of variation

```{r coefficient-variation}
cv_strat <- 100 * se_strat / weighted_mean

cat("Coefficient of variation:",
    round(cv_strat, 3), "%\n")
```

# 8. Naive analysis ignoring the sampling design

The naive analysis treats all 414 sampled students as if they had equal selection probabilities.

```{r naive-analysis}
n_naive <- nrow(sample_data)

naive_mean <- mean(sample_data$pages_month)
naive_sd <- sd(sample_data$pages_month)

# SRSWOR-style variance with finite population correction
naive_var <- (1 - n_naive / N) *
  naive_sd^2 / n_naive

naive_se <- sqrt(naive_var)

naive_lower <- naive_mean - z * naive_se
naive_upper <- naive_mean + z * naive_se

naive_cv <- 100 * naive_se / naive_mean

cat("Naive unweighted mean:",
    round(naive_mean, 4), "\n")
cat("Naive estimated variance:",
    round(naive_var, 6), "\n")
cat("Naive standard error:",
    round(naive_se, 4), "\n")
cat("Naive 95% CI: [",
    round(naive_lower, 3), ",",
    round(naive_upper, 3), "]\n")
cat("Naive CV:",
    round(naive_cv, 3), "%\n")
```

# 9. Difference from the true population mean

```{r estimation-error}
weighted_error <- weighted_mean - true_mean
naive_error <- naive_mean - true_mean

weighted_abs_error <- abs(weighted_error)
naive_abs_error <- abs(naive_error)

cat("Weighted estimate error:",
    round(weighted_error, 3), "pages\n")

cat("Naive estimate error:",
    round(naive_error, 3), "pages\n")

cat("Absolute weighted error:",
    round(weighted_abs_error, 3), "pages\n")

cat("Absolute naive error:",
    round(naive_abs_error, 3), "pages\n")
```

# 10. Design effect

For this report, the variance-based design effect compares the estimated variance under the actual stratified design with the SRSWOR variance that would apply to an equal-sized sample, using the full finite-population variance as the benchmark.

```{r design-effect}
n_design <- nrow(sample_data)

var_srs_benchmark <- (1 - n_design / N) *
  true_variance / n_design

se_srs_benchmark <- sqrt(var_srs_benchmark)

deff <- var_strat / var_srs_benchmark

cat("Stratified design variance:",
    round(var_strat, 6), "\n")

cat("Equal-size SRSWOR benchmark variance:",
    round(var_srs_benchmark, 6), "\n")

cat("Design effect (DEFF):",
    round(deff, 4), "\n")

cat("Relative efficiency (1/DEFF):",
    round(1 / deff, 4), "\n")
```

# 11. Draw an approximately equal-sized SRSWOR sample

A simple random sample without replacement of 414 students is drawn from the complete population. Seed 4105 is used for reproducibility.

```{r draw-srs}
set.seed(4105)

n_srs <- nrow(sample_data)

srs_rows <- sample(
  seq_len(nrow(population)),
  size = n_srs,
  replace = FALSE
)

srs_sample <- population[srs_rows, ]
rownames(srs_sample) <- NULL

srs_sample$inclusion_probability <- n_srs / N
srs_sample$sampling_weight <- N / n_srs

cat("SRSWOR sample size:", nrow(srs_sample), "\n")
cat("Duplicate SRS IDs:",
    sum(duplicated(srs_sample$student_id)), "\n")
```

# 12. Analyse the realised SRSWOR sample

```{r srs-analysis}
srs_mean <- mean(srs_sample$pages_month)
srs_sd <- sd(srs_sample$pages_month)

srs_var_est <- (1 - n_srs / N) *
  srs_sd^2 / n_srs

srs_se <- sqrt(srs_var_est)

srs_lower <- srs_mean - z * srs_se
srs_upper <- srs_mean + z * srs_se

srs_cv <- 100 * srs_se / srs_mean

srs_error <- srs_mean - true_mean

cat("SRSWOR estimated mean:",
    round(srs_mean, 4), "\n")

cat("SRSWOR estimated variance:",
    round(srs_var_est, 6), "\n")

cat("SRSWOR standard error:",
    round(srs_se, 4), "\n")

cat("SRSWOR 95% CI: [",
    round(srs_lower, 3), ",",
    round(srs_upper, 3), "]\n")

cat("SRSWOR CV:",
    round(srs_cv, 3), "%\n")

cat("SRSWOR error from true mean:",
    round(srs_error, 3), "pages\n")
```

# 13. Comparison of the three analyses

```{r comparison-table}
comparison <- data.frame(
  Analysis = c(
    "Stratified design-based",
    "Naive unweighted",
    "Equal-sized SRSWOR"
  ),
  Estimate = c(
    weighted_mean,
    naive_mean,
    srs_mean
  ),
  Variance = c(
    var_strat,
    naive_var,
    srs_var_est
  ),
  SE = c(
    se_strat,
    naive_se,
    srs_se
  ),
  CI_Lower = c(
    ci_lower,
    naive_lower,
    srs_lower
  ),
  CI_Upper = c(
    ci_upper,
    naive_upper,
    srs_upper
  ),
  CV_Percent = c(
    cv_strat,
    naive_cv,
    srs_cv
  ),
  Error_from_True = c(
    weighted_error,
    naive_error,
    srs_error
  )
)

numeric_cols <- sapply(comparison, is.numeric)
comparison[numeric_cols] <-
  round(comparison[numeric_cols], 4)

comparison
```

# 14. Confidence interval comparison plot

```{r ci-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
estimates <- c(
  weighted_mean,
  naive_mean,
  srs_mean
)

lower <- c(
  ci_lower,
  naive_lower,
  srs_lower
)

upper <- c(
  ci_upper,
  naive_upper,
  srs_upper
)

labels <- c(
  "Stratified",
  "Naive",
  "SRSWOR"
)

plot(
  1:3,
  estimates,
  ylim = range(c(lower, upper, true_mean)),
  xaxt = "n",
  xlab = "Analysis",
  ylab = "Estimated mean pages per month",
  main = "Comparison of Estimates and 95% Confidence Intervals",
  pch = 19
)

axis(
  1,
  at = 1:3,
  labels = labels
)

arrows(
  1:3,
  lower,
  1:3,
  upper,
  angle = 90,
  code = 3,
  length = 0.05
)

abline(
  h = true_mean,
  lty = 2
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = "True population mean",
  lty = 2,
  bty = "n"
)
```

# 15. Compare estimated standard errors

```{r se-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
se_values <- c(
  se_strat,
  naive_se,
  srs_se
)

barplot(
  se_values,
  names.arg = c(
    "Stratified",
    "Naive",
    "SRSWOR"
  ),
  ylab = "Estimated standard error",
  main = "Standard Error Comparison"
)
```

# 16. Save SRS sample and Section D results

```{r save-results}
write.csv(
  srs_sample,
  "section_D_srswor_sample.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  comparison,
  "section_D_estimation_comparison.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  stratum_summary,
  "section_D_stratum_estimation_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

```
